grades.quote: `SC.REL` instruction will write the flag of success or failure of its execution (which can be simply understood as the LLbit value seen by the `SC.REL` instruction when it is executed) into the general-purpose register rd and return it, regardless of whether it writes to the memory or not.
grades.reason: This passage covers the acquire/release variants LL.ACQ/SC.REL, not LL.W/SC.W. It does explain the shared LL-SC mechanism. SC writes only if LLbit is 1. ERTN or another core's or coherent master's store to the same cache line clears LLbit. SC returns a success/failure flag in rd. It also notes non-cache-coherent and misalignment cases. It is therefore useful but not a direct answer for SC.W.
